title: Arms Sales Notification
items_summary: Aircraft components, parts, and accessories; spare parts, consumables and accessories, and repair and return support; U.S. Government and contractor engineering, technical, and logistics support services; and other related elements of logistics and program support.
summary: The State Department approved a proposed sale to Greece of aircraft components, spare parts, and repair and return support, plus engineering, technical, and logistics services, with an estimated total cost of $101 million funded by national funds. The sale would improve Greece's ability to sustain its aircraft fleet against modern threats and maintain a constant regional presence, per the policy justification; it contains no Major Defense Equipment and is described as not altering the basic military balance. The principal contractor will be determined through a future contracting process.

DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE

Office of the Secretary

[Transmittal No. 26-86]


Arms Sales Notification

AGENCY: Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA), Department of 
Defense (DoD).

ACTION: Arms sales notice.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY: The DoD (referred to herein as ``the Department,'' 
``Department of War'' or ``DoW'') is publishing the unclassified text 
of an arms sales notification.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Urooj Zahra at (703) 695-6233, 
[email protected], or [email protected].

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: This 36(b) arms sales notification is 
published to fulfill the requirements of section 155 of Public Law 104-
164 dated July 21, 1996. The following is a copy of the attached 
Transmittal 26-86 and Policy Justification.

    Dated: November 17, 2026.
Stephanie J. Bost,
Alternate OSD Federal Register Liaison Officer, Department of Defense.
Transmittal No. 26-86
Notice of Proposed Issuance of Letter of Offer
Pursuant to Section 36(b)(1) of the Arms Export Control Act, as amended
    (i) Prospective Purchaser: Government of Greece
    (ii) Total Estimated Value:

Major Defense Equipment *...............  $0
                                         -------------------------------
Other...................................  $101 million
  TOTAL.................................  $101 million
 

    Funding Source: National Funds
    (iii) Description and Quantity or Quantities of Articles or 
Services under Consideration for Purchase:

Major Defense Equipment (MDE):
    None
Non-MDE:
    Aircraft components, parts, and accessories; spare parts, 
consumables and accessories, and repair and return support; U.S. 
Government and contractor engineering, technical, and logistics support 
services; and other related elements of logistics and program support.

    (iv) Military Department: Air Force (GR-D-KIZ)
    (v) Prior Related Cases, if any: GR-D-KAA
    (vi) Sales Commission, Fee, etc., Paid, Offered, or Agreed to be 
Paid: None known at this time
    (vii) Sensitivity of Technology Contained in the Defense Article or 
Defense Services Proposed to be Sold: None
    (viii) Date Report Delivered to Congress: September 23, 2026
    * as defined in Section 47(6) of the Arms Export Control Act.

POLICY JUSTIFICATION

Greece--Repair and Return Support

    The Government of Greece has requested to buy aircraft components, 
parts, and accessories; spare parts, consumables and accessories, and 
repair and return support; U.S. Government and contractor engineering, 
technical, and logistics support services; and other related elements 
of logistics and program support. The estimated total cost is $101 
million.
    This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national 
security of the United States by improving the security of a NATO Ally 
that continues to be a force for political and economic stability in 
Europe.
    The proposed sale will improve Greece's capability to sustain its 
aircraft fleet to guard against modern threats and maintain a constant 
presence in the region. Greece will have no difficulty absorbing these 
articles and services into its armed forces.
    The proposed sale of this equipment and support will not alter the 
basic military balance in the region.
    The principal contractor will be determined using off-the-shelf 
marketplace or contracting equivalent, request for proposal, or other 
contracting vehicle to ensure the best capabilities at the time of 
contracting. Any offset agreement will be defined in negotiations 
between the purchaser and the contractor.
    Implementation of this proposed sale will not require the 
assignment of any additional U.S. Government or contractor 
representatives to Greece.
    There will be no adverse impact on U.S. defense readiness as a 
result of this proposed sale.
